q-3988.name: Question 1
q-3988.worked_solution:
First, let's rewrite the polynomial equation in the form ${P}_{n}(p)=0.$ To do this, we subtract all the terms from the right-hand side so that the right-hand side becomes $0:$

$$
\begin{aligned}4{p}^{2}+21p & =3{p}^{2}+2{p}^{3} \\ -2{p}^{3}+4{p}^{2}+21p & =3{p}^{2} \\ -2{p}^{3}+{p}^{2}+21p & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Next, notice that all of the terms of the polynomial have a common factor of $-p.$ We can factor out the $-p$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}-2{p}^{3}+{p}^{2}+21p & =0 \\ -p(2{p}^{2}-p-21) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we factor the expression $2{p}^{2}-p-21$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}-p(2{p}^{2}-p-21) & =0 \\ -p(2p-7)(p+3) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, by applying the zero product rule, the solutions are $p=0,$ $p=\frac{7}{2},$ and $p=-3.$

q-3988.html:
Question 1
?

If 4p2+21p=3p2+2p3, then p=

a
p=−3,−72,0
b
p=0,72,3
c
p=−72,0,3
d
p=−3,0,72
e
p=0,32,7
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, let's rewrite the polynomial equation in the form Pn(p)=0. To do this, we subtract all the terms from the right-hand side so that the right-hand side becomes 0: 4p2+21p=3p2+2p3−2p3+4p2+21p=3p2−2p3+p2+21p=0

Next, notice that all of the terms of the polynomial have a common factor of −p. We can factor out the −p as follows: −2p3+p2+21p=0−p(2p2−p−21)=0

Now, we factor the expression 2p2−p−21 as follows: −p(2p2−p−21)=0−p(2p−7)(p+3)=0

Finally, by applying the zero product rule, the solutions are p=0, p=72, and p=−3.

q-37510.name: Question 2
q-37510.problem: Determine the solutions of the equation $10{x}^{3}+2{x}^{2}=\frac{9}{2}x-10{x}^{2}.$
q-37510.worked_solution:
First, let's rewrite the polynomial equation in the form ${P}_{n}(x)=0.$ To do this, we subtract all the terms from the right-hand side so that the right-hand side becomes $0:$

$$
\begin{aligned}10{x}^{3}+2{x}^{2} & =\frac{9}{2}x-10{x}^{2} \\ 10{x}^{3}+12{x}^{2} & =\frac{9}{2}x \\ 10{x}^{3}+12{x}^{2}-\frac{9}{2}x & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we can factor out the $\frac{x}{2}$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}10{x}^{3}+12{x}^{2}-\frac{9}{2}x & =0 \\ \frac{x}{2}(20{x}^{2}+24x-9) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we factor the expression $20{x}^{2}+24x-9$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{x}{2}(20{x}^{2}+24x-9) & =0 \\ \frac{x}{2}(10x-3)(2x+3) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, by applying the zero product rule, the solutions are $x=0,$ $x=\frac{3}{10},$ and $x=-\frac{3}{2}.$

Question 2
?

Determine the solutions of the equation 10x3+2x2=92x−10x2.

a
x=−3,−103,1
b
x=−32,1,310
c
x=−32,−310,0
d
x=−32,0,310
e
x=−310,0,32
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

First, let's rewrite the polynomial equation in the form Pn(x)=0. To do this, we subtract all the terms from the right-hand side so that the right-hand side becomes 0: 10x3+2x2=92x−10x210x3+12x2=92x10x3+12x2−92x=0

Next, we can factor out the x2 as follows: 10x3+12x2−92x=0x2(20x2+24x−9)=0

Now, we factor the expression 20x2+24x−9 as follows: x2(20x2+24x−9)=0x2(10x−3)(2x+3)=0

Finally, by applying the zero product rule, the solutions are x=0, x=310, and x=−32.

q-70465.name: Question 3
q-70465.problem: Find the roots of the polynomial $p(y)=8{y}^{4}+4{y}^{3}-12{y}^{2}.$
q-70465.worked_solution:
To find the roots of the polynomial, we must solve the equation $p(y)=0,$ that is

$$
8{y}^{4}+4{y}^{3}-12{y}^{2}=0.
$$

First, notice that all of the terms of the polynomial have a common factor of $4{y}^{2}.$ We can factor out the $4{y}^{2}$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}4{y}^{2}(2{y}^{2}+y-3) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we factor the expression $2{y}^{2}+y-3$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}4{y}^{2}(2{y}^{2}+y-3) & =0 \\ 4{y}^{2}(2y+3)(y-1) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, by applying the zero product rule, the solutions are $y=0,$ $y=-\frac{3}{2},$ and $y=1.$

q-114115.name: Question 4
q-114115.problem: Find the roots of the polynomial $p(q)=24{q}^{5}-62{q}^{4}+14{q}^{3}.$
q-114115.worked_solution:
To find the roots of the polynomial, we must solve the equation $p(q)=0,$ that is

$$
24{q}^{5}-62{q}^{4}+14{q}^{3}=0.
$$

First, notice that all of the terms of the polynomial have a common factor of $2{q}^{3}.$ We can factor out the $2{q}^{3}$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}2{q}^{3}(12{q}^{2}-31q+7) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we factor the expression $12{q}^{2}-31q+7$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}2{q}^{3}(12{q}^{2}-31q+7) & =0 \\ 2{q}^{3}(4q-1)(3q-7) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

To find the roots of the polynomial, we must solve the equation p(q)=0, that is 24q5−62q4+14q3=0.

First, notice that all of the terms of the polynomial have a common factor of 2q3. We can factor out the 2q3 as follows: 2q3(12q2−31q+7)=0

Now, we factor the expression 12q2−31q+7 as follows: 2q3(12q2−31q+7)=02q3(4q−1)(3q−7)=0

Finally, by applying the zero product rule, the solutions are q=0, q=14, and q=73.
